<div data-hui-table=""><div aria-labelledby="table-deployments-caption" data-hui-table-scroll="" role="region" tabindex="0"><table role="table"><caption id="table-deployments-caption">Deployments</caption><thead role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Application</th><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Deployed</th></tr></thead><tbody role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><td data-label="Application" role="cell">blog</td><td data-label="Deployed" role="cell">2 minutes ago</td></tr></tbody></table></div><nav aria-label="Deployment pages">Page 1 of 2</nav><span data-hui-table-status="" role="status"></span></div>

=== Table / bare, nothing to click ===
a read-only table is still a table: the caption is its name, the roles and scope are all that assistive technology is given, the header-less actions column is hidden rather than announced empty, and the scroll region is focusable even though this table has nothing to click — overflow is the viewport's decision, not the caller's
<div data-hui-table=""><div aria-labelledby="table-recent-deployments-caption" data-hui-table-scroll="" role="region" tabindex="0"><table role="table"><caption id="table-recent-deployments-caption">Recent deployments</caption><thead role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Application</th><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Status</th><th aria-hidden="true" role="columnheader" scope="col"></th></tr></thead><tbody role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><td data-label="Application" role="cell">blog</td><td data-label="Status" role="cell">healthy</td><td role="cell">View</td></tr></tbody></table></div><span data-hui-table-status="" role="status"></span></div>

=== TableOfContents / an observed contents list ===
the entries are real links the server rendered, so the no-script reader gets the whole list, and the module only marks which entry is active
<nav aria-label="&lt;TableOfContentsLabel&gt;" data-hui-toc="" data-hui-toc-target="main"><ol><li><a href="#modeling">Modeling</a></li><li><a href="#serving">Serving</a></li><li><a href="#tuning">Tuning</a></li></ol></nav>

=== TableOfContents / a static contents list ===
with no target the links still work and nothing is marked — the active state is enhancement over a complete list, never the list's only source
<nav aria-label="&lt;TableOfContentsLabel&gt;" data-hui-toc=""><ol><li><a href="#one">One</a></li></ol></nav>

=== TableOfContents / the unlabelled landmark names itself ===
a contents navigation with no label of its own still names its landmark — the default word is the one Strings carries, so a translated page says it in the reader's language
<nav aria-label="&lt;TableOfContentsLabel&gt;" data-hui-toc=""><ol><li><a href="#one">One</a></li></ol></nav>

=== Tabs / a signal tab strip ===
one tab is in the tab order and the rest are reached by the arrows; the panels are real content and the fragment hrefs land on them without script
<div data-active="0" data-fui-signal="cfg" data-fui-signal-attr="data-active" data-fui-signal-mode="attr" data-hui-tabs=""><nav role="tablist"><a aria-controls="cfg-panel-0" aria-selected="true" data-fui-signal-set="cfg:0" data-fui-tab-index="0" href="#cfg-panel-0" id="cfg-tab-0" role="tab" tabindex="0">General</a><a aria-controls="cfg-panel-1" aria-selected="false" data-fui-signal-set="cfg:1" data-fui-tab-index="1" href="#cfg-panel-1" id="cfg-tab-1" role="tab" tabindex="-1">Secrets</a></nav><div><div aria-labelledby="cfg-tab-0" data-fui-tab-index="0" id="cfg-panel-0" role="tabpanel" tabindex="0">The general panel.</div><div aria-labelledby="cfg-tab-1" data-fui-tab-index="1" id="cfg-panel-1" role="tabpanel" tabindex="0">The secrets panel.</div></div></div>

=== Tabs / vacated and stateful ===
hidden panels ship empty with their content in the stash the module restores on first show, and every tab carries the state attribute ports pin locators to
<div data-active="1" data-fui-signal="vac" data-fui-signal-attr="data-active" data-fui-signal-mode="attr" data-hui-tabs="" data-hui-tabs-state="" data-hui-tabs-vacate=""><nav role="tablist"><a aria-controls="vac-panel-0" aria-selected="false" data-fui-signal-set="vac:0" data-fui-tab-index="0" data-state="inactive" href="#vac-panel-0" id="vac-tab-0" role="tab" tabindex="-1">One</a><a aria-controls="vac-panel-1" aria-selected="true" data-fui-signal-set="vac:1" data-fui-tab-index="1" data-state="active" href="#vac-panel-1" id="vac-tab-1" role="tab" tabindex="0">Two</a></nav><div><div aria-labelledby="vac-tab-0" data-fui-tab-index="0" id="vac-panel-0" role="tabpanel" tabindex="0"></div><div aria-labelledby="vac-tab-1" data-fui-tab-index="1" id="vac-panel-1" role="tabpanel" tabindex="0">Second panel.</div><script data-hui-tabs-stash="true" type="application/json">{"0":"First panel."}</script></div></div>

=== Tag / removable ===
the × names what it removes — twelve controls all called Remove tell a screen reader user nothing — and it is an anchor that keeps its href for no script while carrying the island contract, because dropping a filter is an in-page state change and never a route
<span>env=prod<a aria-label="&lt;RemoveLabelled env=prod&gt;" data-fui-push-state="/apps?env=" data-fui-rpc="/island/apps?env=" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" href="/apps?env=">×</a></span>

=== Tag / fixed ===
a tag with nothing to navigate to renders no control at all rather than a dead ×, and its icon is hidden from assistive technology exactly as a badge's is, because a tag is a badge with a dismiss control and the two must not drift
<span><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span>leader</span>

=== TagInput / values, visible and submittable ===
every committed value is a chip with its own named remove control AND a hidden input — what a reader sees removed is what a submit stops carrying, on the first paint, with no module at all
<div aria-label="Tags" data-hui-tag-input="tags" data-hui-tag-input-remove-label="&lt;RemoveLabelled %s&gt;" role="group"><label for="tags">Tags</label><div><ul data-hui-tag-input-list="" role="list"><li aria-label="&lt;RemoveLabelled go&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-remove="">go<button aria-label="&lt;RemoveLabelled go&gt;" type="button">×</button><input name="tags" type="hidden" value="go"></li><li aria-label="&lt;RemoveLabelled css&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-remove="">css<button aria-label="&lt;RemoveLabelled css&gt;" type="button">×</button><input name="tags" type="hidden" value="css"></li></ul><input aria-label="Tags" autocomplete="off" data-hui-tag-input-field="" id="tags" type="text"><button aria-label="&lt;TagInputAdd Tags&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-add="" type="button">+</button></div><span data-hui-tag-input-added="&lt;TagInputAdded {name}&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-removed="&lt;TagInputRemoved {name}&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-status="" role="status"></span></div>

=== TagInput / an empty list with a draft field ===
an empty tag field still renders its list and its status wiring, so the module that binds the field arrives to a page shaped like the one it expects
<div aria-label="Topics" data-hui-tag-input="topics" data-hui-tag-input-remove-label="&lt;RemoveLabelled %s&gt;" role="group"><label for="topics">Topics</label><div><ul data-hui-tag-input-list="" role="list"></ul><input aria-label="Topics" autocomplete="off" data-hui-tag-input-field="" id="topics" placeholder="Type a topic" type="text"><button aria-label="&lt;TagInputAdd Topics&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-add="" type="button">+</button></div><span data-hui-tag-input-added="&lt;TagInputAdded {name}&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-removed="&lt;TagInputRemoved {name}&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-status="" role="status"></span></div>

=== TagInput / a capped, helped field ===
the cap rides both the draft input and the rendered values — a server value longer than the cap cannot submit unchanged while a typed one is refused — and the rule rides the field's own description
<div aria-label="Labels" data-hui-tag-input="labels" data-hui-tag-input-maxlength="8" data-hui-tag-input-remove-label="&lt;RemoveLabelled %s&gt;" role="group"><label for="labels">Labels</label><div><ul data-hui-tag-input-list="" role="list"><li aria-label="&lt;RemoveLabelled prod&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-remove="">prod<button aria-label="&lt;RemoveLabelled prod&gt;" type="button">×</button><input name="labels" type="hidden" value="prod"></li></ul><input aria-label="Labels" autocomplete="off" data-hui-tag-input-field="" id="labels" maxlength="8" type="text"><button aria-label="&lt;TagInputAdd Labels&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-add="" type="button">+</button></div><span data-hui-tag-input-added="&lt;TagInputAdded {name}&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-removed="&lt;TagInputRemoved {name}&gt;" data-hui-tag-input-status="" role="status"></span><p>One word each, eight characters at most.</p></div>

=== Textarea / with content ===
the value is the element's text, not an attribute — which is why it is the one control whose content must be escaped rather than quoted
<textarea id="notes" name="notes">Restarted after the 4am alert.</textarea>

=== Textarea / growing ===
autogrow is the one core-runtime hook a control here renders — the behaviour belongs to the control, and the prop is the only seam that survives the prefix refusal
<div><label for="notes-grow">Release notes</label><textarea data-fui-autogrow="" id="notes-grow" name="notes">Grows to fit whatever is typed.</textarea></div>

=== Timeline / history ===
an event with no tone is the ordinary case and draws an untinted marker; ordered, because the order is the content: a screen reader announces the count and the position, so "3 of 7" locates you in the history without seeing the line down the left
<ol aria-label="Deploy history"><li><span aria-hidden="true"></span><div><time datetime="2026-09-08T11:04:00Z">3 days ago</time><p>Deployed</p><p>From main, by Donald.</p></div></li><li><span aria-hidden="true"></span><div><time datetime="2026-09-07T09:12:00Z">4 days ago</time><p>Build failed</p><p>Exit 1 in the test stage.</p></div></li><li><span aria-hidden="true"></span><div><time datetime="2026-09-06T16:40:00Z">5 days ago</time><p>Configuration changed</p></div></li></ol>

=== Timeline / attributed ===
the meta line qualifies the title from the same row — an actor or a relative time — and the title stays first in the tree so a reader hears the event before its attribution
<ol aria-label="Audit log"><li><span aria-hidden="true"></span><div><div><p>Role granted</p><span>by dom</span></div><p>admin, on the api app.</p></div></li></ol>

=== Toast / a success, visible with no script ===
the toast row is on the first paint — a notification the server rendered is news already delivered, and no module is needed to read it
<div data-hui-toast=""><span>&lt;ToneSuccess&gt;: </span><span aria-hidden="true">✓</span><span>Deploy finished</span><span>api is serving build 482</span></div>

=== Toast / assertive, with a dismiss that keeps its href ===
the failure a reader must hear carries role=alert on its own row inside the politely-announcing stack, and the dismiss link needs its Island at render because dropping a notification is an in-page state change, never a route
<div data-hui-toast="" data-hui-toast-ttl-ms="8000" role="alert"><span>&lt;ToneDanger&gt;: </span><span>Connection lost</span><a aria-label="&lt;DismissTitled Connection lost&gt;" data-fui-push-state="/dismiss/conn" data-fui-rpc="/island/toasts" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="toasts" data-hui-toast-dismiss="" href="/dismiss/conn">×</a></div>

=== ToastStack / the stack with its rows ===
one region a layout mounts once: the runtime's header path inserts into it, the server's rows are already in it, and its name is what a reader jumps by
<div aria-label="Notifications" data-fui-toast-stack="Notifications" data-hui-toast-dismiss-label="&lt;DismissTitled %s&gt;" data-hui-toast-max="4" data-hui-toast-stack="" data-hui-toast-tone-danger="&lt;ToneDanger&gt;" data-hui-toast-tone-info="&lt;ToneInfo&gt;" data-hui-toast-tone-success="&lt;ToneSuccess&gt;" data-hui-toast-tone-warning="&lt;ToneWarning&gt;" role="region"><div data-hui-toast=""><span>&lt;ToneSuccess&gt;: </span><span>Saved</span></div></div>

=== ToastStack / empty, the wiring still there ===
an empty stack still renders, because the module that injects runtime toasts needs the region to exist — a stack that vanishes when empty is a stack the first toast has to rebuild
<div aria-label="Notifications" data-fui-toast-stack="Notifications" data-hui-toast-dismiss-label="&lt;DismissTitled %s&gt;" data-hui-toast-stack="" data-hui-toast-tone-danger="&lt;ToneDanger&gt;" data-hui-toast-tone-info="&lt;ToneInfo&gt;" data-hui-toast-tone-success="&lt;ToneSuccess&gt;" data-hui-toast-tone-warning="&lt;ToneWarning&gt;" role="region"></div>

=== ToggleAction / idle ===
aria-pressed false and the committed span hidden: first paint matches the server's answer, and the runtime only ever flips what is already there
<button aria-pressed="false" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/apps/blog/watch" data-hui-action-failed="&lt;ActionFailed&gt;" data-state="idle" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="">Watch</span><span data-hui-action-done="" hidden="">Watching</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== ToggleAction / committed at load ===
the server knows: aria-pressed is true and it is the idle span that is hidden, so a page that loads already-watching does not flash through the wrong label first — and each label carries its own aria-hidden icon, so the flip swaps glyph and word together
<button aria-pressed="true" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/apps/blog/watch" data-hui-action-failed="&lt;ActionFailed&gt;" data-state="committed" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="" hidden=""><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span>Watch</span><span data-hui-action-done=""><span aria-hidden="true"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.25"/><path d="M5.5 8.25 7.25 10l3.25-3.5"/></svg></span>Watching</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== ToggleAction / unwatch, not post ===
a method other than POST is published as an attribute, because the primitive defaults to POST and an unstated DELETE would fire the wrong request entirely — the same rule the optimistic button's delete case states
<button aria-pressed="true" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/apps/blog/watch" data-hui-action-failed="&lt;ActionFailed&gt;" data-hui-action-method="DELETE" data-state="committed" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="" hidden="">Watch</span><span data-hui-action-done="">Watching</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== ToggleAction / two in a mutex group ===
committing one member of a group revokes the other with no second request, so a plan picker reads as one choice rather than three independent buttons that can all be on
<button aria-pressed="true" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/plan/starter" data-hui-action-failed="&lt;ActionFailed&gt;" data-hui-action-group="plan" data-state="committed" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="" hidden="">Starter</span><span data-hui-action-done="">Starter ✓</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button><button aria-pressed="false" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/plan/pro" data-hui-action-failed="&lt;ActionFailed&gt;" data-hui-action-group="plan" data-state="idle" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="">Pro</span><span data-hui-action-done="" hidden="">Pro ✓</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== ToggleAction / untoggle, with its own endpoint ===
a committed button that can be clicked again publishes the untoggle endpoint and ships committed — the only state from which untoggle is reachable — so the revert is a request the server can refuse, not just a local flip
<button aria-pressed="true" data-hui-action="" data-hui-action-endpoint="/plan/pro" data-hui-action-failed="&lt;ActionFailed&gt;" data-hui-action-untoggle="/plan/none" data-state="committed" type="button"><span data-hui-action-idle="" hidden="">Pro</span><span data-hui-action-done="">Pro ✓</span><span data-hui-action-status="" role="status"></span></button>

=== Toolbar / controls in a row ===
no role=toolbar: that role promises arrow-key roving with a single tab stop, and a promise a script-free component cannot keep is worse than saying nothing
<div><button type="button">New app</button><button type="button">Refresh</button></div>

=== ToolbarGroup / labelled group ===
the label names what the group of controls acts on, so the controls inside can stay short without becoming ambiguous
<div><span>Sort</span><button type="button">Name</button></div>

=== ToolbarSearch / search slot ===
the search field is the one control in a toolbar that should grow, so its wrapper is the GET form that submits it — an island update with script, the page's own query without
<form data-fui-rpc="/island/apps" data-fui-rpc-method="GET" data-fui-rpc-signal="apps" method="get"><input aria-label="Search apps" name="q" type="search"></form>

=== ToolbarSpacer / gap ===
an empty element that pushes what follows to the far end — it renders nothing, says nothing, and is in the markup only because the layout needs a thing to grow
<div></div>

=== ValidationSummary / after a failed submit ===
it interrupts and can take focus, and every error is a link to the field it is about — a list of complaints you cannot navigate to is a list you have to hunt through
<div aria-labelledby="errors-title" id="errors" role="alert" tabindex="-1"><h2 id="errors-title">This form could not be saved</h2><ul><li><a href="#name">Enter an app name.</a></li><li><a href="#port">Port 8080 is already in use.</a></li></ul></div>

=== ValidationSummary / an error with no field ===
"the registry rejected the push" belongs to no input, and dropping it because it has nowhere to link would lose the only message that explains the failure
<div aria-labelledby="errors2-title" id="errors2" role="alert" tabindex="-1"><h2 id="errors2-title">This form could not be saved</h2><ul><li>The registry rejected the push.</li></ul></div>

=== ValidationSummary / nothing wrong ===
no errors renders nothing at all, so a page can ask for the summary unconditionally and not get an empty red box on first load
<p>Nothing to report.</p>

=== ValidationSummary / two summaries on one page ===
two forms that failed on one page label two summaries, and the required ids are what keep the titles from sharing one name — the reference gate reads both labels and both resolve to their own heading
<div aria-labelledby="errors-left-title" id="errors-left" role="alert" tabindex="-1"><h2 id="errors-left-title">&lt;ThereIsAProblem&gt;</h2><ul><li><a href="#left-name">Enter a name.</a></li></ul></div><div aria-labelledby="errors-right-title" id="errors-right" role="alert" tabindex="-1"><h2 id="errors-right-title">&lt;ThereIsAProblem&gt;</h2><ul><li><a href="#right-name">Enter a name.</a></li></ul></div>
